pages.title: From AI experiments to governed capability
pages.subtitle: A practical operating model for making better decisions, proving value and retaining control

pages.title: The constraint is rarely a shortage of ideas
pages.dek: Organisations need a disciplined way to decide what deserves investment and what evidence is required before scale.

blocks.text: AI activity becomes valuable when it is connected to decisions, operating realities and accountable ownership.

Many teams can produce a compelling demonstration. Fewer can explain how the capability will work with real data, existing controls, frontline practice and the people responsible for outcomes. That gap is where promising experiments often stall.

A better model treats each initiative as a sequence of evidence-building decisions. It makes assumptions visible, tests the highest-risk claims first and creates a clear threshold for continuing, changing direction or stopping.

blocks.label: Core principle
blocks.title: Governance should improve the decision, not merely document it.
blocks.body: The useful question is not whether a project passed a generic gate. It is whether the available evidence justifies the next commitment of money, data, operational attention and trust.

pages.title: Move from enthusiasm to evidence
pages.summary: A small number of explicit decisions can turn a loose portfolio of experiments into a governed learning system.

pages.title: A repeatable path from question to capability
pages.dek: The sequence is stable even when the technology, business function and level of ambition change.

columns.text: Define what must be decided, who owns that decision and what would make the answer useful. This prevents a technology demonstration from becoming the objective.

items: Name the operational outcome and current constraint.
Separate confirmed facts from assumptions and unknowns.
Agree the evidence required for the next commitment.

columns.label: Decision quality
columns.title: A useful stop is a successful outcome.
columns.body: Stopping weak work early protects attention for initiatives that can withstand scrutiny.

items.title: Frame
items.body: State the business decision, scope, owner and material constraints.

items.title: Test
items.body: Design the cheapest credible test of the most consequential assumption.

items.title: Observe
items.body: Capture user, operational, technical and control evidence separately.

items.title: Decide
items.body: Continue, reshape or stop using a threshold agreed before the test.

items.title: Industrialise
items.body: Add service ownership, monitoring, support and change only after value is evidenced.

pages.title: Keep different kinds of evidence distinct
pages.dek: A technically successful test does not, by itself, establish operational value or permission to scale.

rows: Representative users complete the real task with an agreed improvement.
Ownership, exception handling and support are exercised in context.
Performance, security and failure paths pass defined thresholds.
Is the value worth the full cost?
Benefits and ongoing costs are evidenced with stated assumptions.
Required legal, risk, data and stakeholder approvals are recorded.
blocks.caption: Illustrative evidence categories. The applicable acceptance signals should be agreed for each initiative.

blocks.label: Release discipline
blocks.title: Build success is not operational acceptance.
blocks.body: Keep test evidence, provider status, organisational approval and live operating proof as separate gates.

pages.title: Make the portfolio legible
pages.dek: Leadership should be able to see what is known, what is being tested and what decision comes next.

items.label: Named decision owner
items.note: One accountable person for the next decision

blocks.text: A useful portfolio view is concise. It should identify the decision being made, the current evidence, the largest unresolved risk, the next test and the owner. Activity counts are secondary because they do not show whether uncertainty is actually reducing.
Progress is evidence that changes a decision, not activity that fills a status report.

items: Use a common evidence language across initiatives.
Record failed assumptions and negative findings, not only successes.
Require fresh operating proof before describing a capability as live.

pages.title: Know what is real. Know what to do next.
pages.body: We help enterprise teams examine AI opportunities, test the claims that matter and turn justified choices into governed delivery.
